minor.issue: Brute-force lockout does NOT accumulate behind Kubernetes ingress. Key uses request.client.host which is the proxy IP (same for every request), so counts should build — but observed 7 consecutive failed attempts all return 401 (never 429). Likely each request lands on a different pod/worker without shared state OR the mongo write is racing. Recommend keying on X-Forwarded-For (client IP header) AND ensure single-writer semantics; also consider capping to 5 in a rolling 15-min window explicitly.

rca of the issue: Brute-force lockout RCA: server.py:248 uses `ip = request.client.host if request.client else '?'` as part of key. Behind K8s ingress, request.client.host reflects the ingress/service proxy (or load balancer), not the true remote client. When counter accumulates it may be shared across all requests from that proxy, so effectively works — BUT observed behavior in test was 7 x 401 in a row, suggesting either the counter write is not persisting (unlikely — motor upsert is atomic) or the read/write scheduling in the async loop somehow keeps count<5. Reproduction: `for i in $(seq 1 7); do curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -X POST $BASE/api/auth/login -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"email":"x@example.com","password":"y"}'; done` → all 401. Mitigation: extract client IP from X-Forwarded-For header and enforce lockout on that combined with email; consider also a per-email global lockout to avoid IP-hopping bypass.
